```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, message = FALSE)
has_gg <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
```

Small-area mortality forecasts are usually needed at several levels at once:
for each sex, region and deprivation quintile, and for their totals (a
region for both sexes, a quintile nationally, the whole country). Forecasts
made separately for each of these strata do not add up. This vignette shows
how mortensor produces coherent forecasts for such a grouped (crossed)
structure.

*The data here are simulated with `mt_example_regions()` (2 sexes x 4
regions x 5 quintiles); the vignette will be rerun with real data.*

```{r}
library(mortensor)
library(data.table)
x <- mt_example_regions(years = 1990:2019, regions = 4)
x
```

## The hierarchy

Deaths and exposures add up over strata, rates do not. A hierarchy lists the
stratum variables that are aggregated and the label of their totals.
Intermediate groups (for example regions grouped into larger areas) are
given with `groups`.

```{r}
h <- mt_hierarchy(sex = "both", region = "all", quintile = "all")
h
xa <- mt_aggregate_strata(x, h)
nrow(mt_strata(xa))
tail(mt_strata(xa))
```

The aggregated data have 90 strata: 40 bottom series and 50 aggregates. If
official totals are available as data, they can be supplied as strata of
their own, and `mt_validate()` checks that they agree with the sums of their
parts:

```{r}
mt_validate(xa, hierarchy = h)
```

## Three ways to coherent forecasts

1. **A joint model, aggregated bottom-up.** `li_lee(common_by = "sex")` fits
   one common trend per sex from the pooled bottom strata, and lets regions
   and quintiles deviate from it with stationary (AR(1)) factors, so their
   gaps neither vanish nor explode. Aggregates are sums of the bottom
   forecasts (`method = "bottom_up"`).
2. **Separate models, reconciled.** Any model is fitted to every node
   (bottom and aggregates) and the forecasts are projected onto the coherent
   subspace draw by draw (`method = "wls"`, `"mint"`, `"structural"`,
   `"ols"`). Because separately fitted strata have independent draws, the
   draws are first reordered along the co-movement observed in the training
   data (an empirical copula), otherwise the aggregates would be too
   certain.
3. **No reconciliation**: the base forecasts, for comparison.

`mt_reconciled()` wraps a model so that reconciliation is part of every fit,
also inside backtests.

```{r}
specs <- list(
  lee_carter(),
  mt_reconciled(lee_carter(), h, method = "wls"),
  li_lee(common_by = "sex"),
  mt_reconciled(li_lee(common_by = "sex"), h, method = "bottom_up"))
hs <- mortensor:::hierarchy_structure(mt_strata(xa), h)
level <- ifelse(hs$is_bottom, "bottom", "aggregate")
bt <- rbindlist(lapply(specs, function(sp) {
  b <- mt_backtest(sp, xa, origins = c(2005, 2008), h = 10, n_draws = 200)
  b[, level := level[stratum]]
}))
dcast(bt[, .(crps = round(mean(crps), 4), cov95 = round(mean(cov95), 3)), by = .(model, level)],
      model ~ level, value.var = c("crps", "cov95"))
```

On these data the joint model aggregated bottom-up is both coherent and the
most accurate. Reconciling separate Lee-Carter fits makes them coherent with
well calibrated intervals at every level, at a small cost in accuracy of the
aggregates.

## Forecasts at every level

```{r}
fit <- mt_fit(mt_reconciled(li_lee(common_by = "sex"), h, method = "bottom_up"), xa)
fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 15, n_draws = 500, seed = 1)
fc$reconciliation
```

```{r, eval = has_gg}
mt_plot_forecast(fc, ages = c("60-64", "75-79"), strata = c("both.all.Q1", "both.all.Q5", "both.all.all"))
```

Path-by-path quantities stay coherent too, for example the deprivation gap
in the probability of dying between ages 40 and 75:

```{r}
p <- prob_dying(fc, from = 40, to = 75)
p[sex == "both" & region == "all" & quintile %in% c("Q1", "Q5") & period %in% c(2020, 2034),
  .(quintile, period, q0.025, q0.5, q0.975)]
```

## Future populations

Reconciliation on deaths uses exposures for the forecast years. By default
these are the exposures of the last observed year; external population
projections can be supplied as `exposure` to `mt_forecast()` and
`mt_reconcile()` (an array `[age, year, stratum]`; only the bottom strata are
used, aggregates are summed).
